What Shizuku is

Shizuku is a free app that lets other apps use system functions with the rights of the debugging shell. EtherTether needs it for one thing: asking Android to start or stop Ethernet tethering. Shizuku is a separate project and not part of EtherTether.
1. Install Shizuku
Download Shizuku from its official page. The page opens in your browser.
Shizuku is installed.
Open the official Shizuku page
Open Shizuku
2. Start Shizuku with wireless debugging
This needs no computer. Pairing is needed only once.
Connect the phone to any Wi-Fi network. Wireless debugging needs Wi-Fi, but no internet.
Turn on Developer options: open Settings, About phone, and tap Build number seven times. On Xiaomi phones tap OS version instead.
Open Shizuku and tap Pairing in the section about wireless debugging. Shizuku shows a notification.
In Developer options, open Wireless debugging, turn it on and tap Pair device with pairing code.
Type the pairing code into the Shizuku notification.
Go back to Shizuku and tap Start.
Step %1$d
Open Developer options
3. Allow EtherTether
Come back here and tap Grant access. Shizuku asks you to allow EtherTether.
After every restart
Shizuku stops when the phone restarts. Open Shizuku and tap Start again; you do not need to pair again.
